# A dock composition that omits the tear-out boundary gets header-clamped tab drags

## The defect

`dashboard.dock.projection.LayoutAdapter` forwards `boundaryContainerId` into each tabs node's header `sortZoneConfig` **only when the composition passes `dockTearOutBoundaryContainerId`** (LayoutAdapter.mjs ~1023). Every composition that omits it falls back to the generic container default — `container.Base#afterSetSortable` creates the sort zone with `boundaryContainerId: me.id`, the header toolbar's own element — and the base SortZone clamps the drag proxy to that boundary's rect.

Result for a dock host: a tab drag that begins as an in-header sort can never leave the header strip. The proxy pins to the toolbar, and the cross-zone machinery the same zone is supposed to drive degrades — measured on a consumer: the drop indicators render parked and degenerate at the dock corner (w≈11px at the strip's edge) instead of tracking the pointer. A drag that exits the strip on its very first move happens to engage the cross-zone path, which makes the failure look intermittent and gesture-dependent.

`apps/workstation` never sees this because it passes `dockTearOutBoundaryContainerId: me.id` (view/Workspace.mjs ~948) — its comment even states the intended semantics: *"Exiting a source toolbar remains ordinary cross-zone motion; only leaving this app/window root enters the vessel outcome machine."* The first external consumer omitted the option — its name says **tear-out**, an opt-in feature — and got clamped drags on day one. Witnessed live in a private consumer workspace on current `dev`; one line (passing the option) fully restores both gesture shapes.

The adapter's fallback comment says omitting the option keeps consumers "byte-identical" — byte-identical to a *plain tab container*, but for a dock composition the toolbar clamp contradicts the product's core interaction. An option named for tear-out silently governs basic in-window cross-zone drag UX.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `dashboard.dock.Workspace`-backed composition that passes no tear-out options gets tab-header sort zones whose drag boundary is the dock workspace root (the Workspace auto-supplies its component id per the ledger); tear-out stays opt-in and plain `tab.Container` behavior stays untouched. A direct `LayoutAdapter.project()` consumer owns supplying the workspace-boundary context field itself — omitting both keys retains the header-toolbar clamp for that consumer class, and the option's docs state exactly that.
- [ ] A spec pins the sort-first gesture shape: pointer moves within the strip first, then exits — the cross-zone preview/indicators must engage at the pointer, not park at the strip.
- [ ] `dockTearOutBoundaryContainerId` docs state which behaviors it governs beyond tear-out, or the boundary default moves out of its shadow so it governs only tear-out.

## Contract Ledger (consumed cells)

| Cell | Producer | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (1) tear-out boundary **omitted** (today's default) | `container.Base#afterSetSortable` merges `boundaryContainerId: me.id` (the header toolbar) under `sortZoneConfig`; `projection.LayoutAdapter` omits the key entirely when `context.dockTearOutBoundaryContainerId` is null (~:1023) | Proxy clamped to the tab-strip rect (`main.addon.DragDrop` boundary clamp, ~:914), with `allowOverdrag: false` (gated on `enableDockTearOut`, ~:1040) — the adapter's own §2.8 comment states the consequence: "while the proxy is clamped to the tab-strip boundary the intersection ratio never drops — the exit cannot fire". Sort-first gestures cannot leave the strip; cross-zone previews degrade (indicators parked degenerate at the strip corner, w≈11px) | None — silent | The adapter comment calls the fallback "byte-identical" for consumers that omit the option; true only relative to plain tab containers, not to dock semantics | Consumer repro (sort-first vs fast-exit gesture, measured); `apps/workstation` immune because it supplies the option |
| (2) `dockTearOutBoundaryContainerId` **supplied** | Composition option → `LayoutAdapter` ~:1023-1025 → `sortZoneConfig.boundaryContainerId` | Proxy free within the named root; exiting a source toolbar is ordinary cross-zone motion. This key alone does NOT arm tear-out — arming is `enableDockTearOut === true`, which pairs `allowOverdrag` + `enableProxyToPopup` + the window-boundary hysteresis (~:1040-1042) | n/a | `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` ~:948 comment (the §2.8 block) states the intended semantics | Workstation (long-standing); the consumer fix passed ONLY this key with tear-out off — cross-zone motion restored, tear-out never armed, both gesture shapes re-verified |
| (3) **Selected mechanic for this ticket** | `dashboard.dock.Workspace` supplies its OWN component id into the projection context as the boundary default (a new context field alongside the existing options; el id = component id by the component contract, so it is a real DOM id, unlike `context.workspaceId`, which is `options.workspaceId ?? null` — an optional input nothing produces). The adapter resolves `sortZoneConfig.boundaryContainerId` as explicit `dockTearOutBoundaryContainerId` first, then the new context field. **Direct-adapter consumers** (compositions building `LayoutAdapter` without `dashboard.dock.Workspace`): the field is part of the ADAPTER's options contract and such a consumer owns supplying it — omitting BOTH keys retains today's toolbar clamp for that consumer class only, and the option's docs must say exactly that (the adapter owns no component, so it cannot manufacture a root id) | Omitted-option compositions get workspace-bounded drags — cell (1) collapses into cell (2) with root = workspace. Supplying the option stays byte-identical. Tear-out arming unchanged (still `enableDockTearOut`). Explicitly NOT via `allowOverdrag`: that flag is tear-out's pairing switch — flipping it without tear-out removes the in-window clamp semantics instead of widening them. Explicitly NOT via changing `container.Base`'s generic default: plain toolbars keep their clamp | The generic toolbar clamp remains for non-dock sortables | AC-3 already covers documenting which behaviors the option name governs, or moving the boundary default out of its shadow | The consumer fix IS this mechanic applied manually (one composition line); the AC-2 spec pins the sort-first gesture shape so the default cannot regress |
